source: verified open-source software for graphic-design->hardware (design->toolpath, firmware, host).

components.name: svg2gcode
components.what: Rust library and CLI that converts SVG vector graphics into G-code for pen plotters, laser engravers, and other CNC machines.

components.name: vpype
components.what: Python command-line "Swiss Army knife" that reads/optimizes SVG vector artwork (line sorting, layout, occlusion, generative ops) as the pipeline stage before G-code output.

components.name: vpype-gcode
components.what: vpype plugin that writes G-code (and other configurable ASCII toolpath formats) from the processed vector geometry via customizable output profiles.

components.name: juicy-gcode
components.what: Haskell command-line tool that converts SVG into optimized G-code, notable for biarc curve fitting (as well as linear and cubic-bezier approximation) for smooth plotter/CNC toolpaths.

components.name: gcodetools (Inkscape extension)
components.what: CAM extension for Inkscape that exports drawn/selected paths to G-code (area fill, engraving, lathe, tool libraries), converting an SVG design directly into CNC toolpaths from inside the editor.

components.name: LinuxCNC image-to-gcode (image2gcode)
components.what: Standalone Python filter bundled with LinuxCNC that turns a greyscale raster image into a Z-depth map and generates 2.5D milling G-code (brightness = cut depth), with roughing-pass support.

components.name: LaserGRBL
components.what: Actively maintained Windows GUI for GRBL controllers that imports raster images (JPG/BMP/PNG) and vectors, generates laser G-code line-by-line (dithering/grayscale/vectorize), then streams it to the machine.

components.name: GRBL
components.what: The classic open-source G-code parser and CNC motion controller written in optimized C, generating up to 30 kHz jitter-free step pulses with look-ahead acceleration.

components.name: grblHAL
components.what: A hardware-abstraction-layer rewrite of grbl 1.1f that runs the same core on 32-bit MCUs with a plugin architecture, driven by separate per-chip driver repos.

components.name: FluidNC
components.what: The next-generation ESP32 CNC firmware from the grbl/grblESP32 lineage, configured via runtime YAML (no recompile) with a built-in WiFi web UI.

components.name: Marlin
components.what: The dominant open-source RepRap 3D-printer firmware for 8- and 32-bit MCUs, which also ships built-in laser and CNC spindle (G-code) control for those machine types.

components.name: Universal Gcode Sender (UGS)
components.what: Java-based cross-platform G-code sender for GRBL/FluidNC (plus TinyG, g2core, Smoothieware) with a dedicated jog controller panel, DRO, and 3D visualizer.
components.capability: host / G-code sender (streams G-code over USB)

components.name: bCNC
components.what: Advanced Python/Tkinter G-code sender for GRBL/grblHAL with jogging, auto-leveling (probe height map), a G-code editor, and CAM tools, runs well on low-power hardware like Raspberry Pi.
components.capability: host / G-code sender (streams G-code over USB)

components.name: CNCjs
components.what: Node.js web-based CNC controller/G-code sender for GRBL, Marlin, Smoothieware, and TinyG, with a browser jog UI, 6-axis DRO, keyboard shortcuts, pendant support, and 3D toolpath view.
components.capability: host / G-code sender (streams G-code over USB)

components.name: OpenBuilds CONTROL
components.what: Electron-based GRBL host/interface and G-code sender for CNC machines (GRBL and GRBL-compatible like FluidNC) with jogging, probing wizards, and job streaming.
components.capability: host / G-code sender (streams G-code over USB)

components.name: GRBL firmware
components.what: Option A motion-control firmware flashed onto the Uno; parses G-code and does the real-time step-pulse generation for both axes.

components.name: FluidNC firmware
components.what: Option B GRBL-compatible motion firmware for the ESP32; adds WiFi control, an SD-card config file, and native multi-driver (TMC2209 UART) support.
